territorial_scope.description: State statute of Arizona; the operator definition covers persons offering conversational AI services to the public, and the text states no express territorial limit.

evidence.quote: A PERSON THAT DEVELOPS AND MAKES AVAILABLE A CONVERSATIONAL AI SERVICE TO THE PUBLIC.

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Introduced Arizona bill adding chapter 8 on conversational AI services. Operators must disclose AI interaction to minor account holders, prevent sexual and human-simulating statements to minors, offer privacy tools, adopt suicide-response protocols, and not represent services as mental health care. Attorney General enforces civil penalties; effective September 30, 2027.
summary.long: HB 2311 would add chapter 8 to Title 18 of the Arizona Revised Statutes, regulating operators that develop and make available to the public a conversational AI service: AI software or web interfaces that primarily simulate human conversation, excluding developer-, research-, narrow-topic-, business-only, embedded and voice-assistant products. Operators must clearly disclose AI interaction to minor account holders (as a persistent disclaimer, or at session start and at least every three hours) and where a reasonable person would be misled. They must not give minors unpredictable reward incentives to increase engagement, must take reasonable measures to prevent sexual visual material, sexual statements and human-simulating or romantic statements to minors, must offer privacy and account tools to minor account holders and, for those under thirteen, their parents or guardians, must adopt a protocol for suicidal ideation or self-harm prompts including referral to crisis services, and must not knowingly represent that the service is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care. A violation is subject to injunction and liability for the greater of actual damages or civil penalties of $1,000 per violation, not exceeding $500,000 per operator. Civil penalties are sought only by the Attorney General, and the section creates no private right of action. The chapter is effective from and after September 30, 2027.

relations.note: The bill adds Chapter 8 (Sections 18-801 and 18-802) to Title 18 as new text.

notes: Bill text as introduced; the document contains no legislative history. Section 1 adds new text only. Section 18-802(I) makes an operator liable for the greater of actual damages or civil penalties, while 18-802(J) provides that the civil penalty is sought by the attorney general only and creates no private right of action; the text does not reconcile these provisions. Section 2 sets the effective date as from and after September 30, 2027. The definitions of sexual conduct and visual depiction depend on A.R.S. 13-3551, which is not reproduced here.

thresholds.variable_text: age of an individual, under eighteen years of age (minor definition)
thresholds.measurement: Operator's actual knowledge or reasonable certainty of the individual's age; the operator determines status.
thresholds.consequence: An individual under eighteen is a minor for this chapter, so the minor-specific duties in 18-802 apply to the operator.
thresholds.conditions: Operator has actual knowledge or reasonable certainty that the individual is under eighteen.

thresholds.variable_text: age of a minor account holder, under thirteen years of age
thresholds.value_text: IS UNDER THIRTEEN YEARS OF AGE
thresholds.measurement: Age of the minor account holder as known to the operator under the minor definition.
thresholds.consequence: The operator must also offer privacy and account setting tools to the account holder's parent or guardian.
thresholds.conditions: Account holder is a minor account holder.

evidence.quote: IF THE ACCOUNT HOLDER IS UNDER THIRTEEN YEARS OF AGE

thresholds.variable_text: age of a minor account holder, thirteen years of age or above
thresholds.value_text: THIRTEEN YEARS OF AGE OR ABOVE
thresholds.measurement: Age of the minor account holder as known to the operator under the minor definition.
thresholds.consequence: The operator must offer related tools to the parent or guardian, as appropriate based on relevant risks.
thresholds.conditions: Account holder is a minor account holder.
